spans.s:
Arhat
(‘venerable’)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the verbal root ‘arh’ (‘to deserve’) the word ‘Arhat’ is common to both बुद्धिस्म् and जैनिस्म्. However it is in जैनिस्म् that it is more current.
The Arhats (also spelt as Arahats or Arahantas) are beings who have become perfect and can teach the way to perfection to others. They are endowed with un-limited knowledge, vision, power and bliss. They are free from the limitations of flesh like hunger or thirst, since their bodies are not material. ‘Jina’ is another name commonly applied to them.
In the Pañcaparameṣṭhi-mantra the Arhats are the first to whom obeisance is offered (ṇamo arihantāṇam).
